data.cultural_impact: The name Kholah carries a deep cultural significance as it embodies the strong and cherished role of women in Islamic society as caregivers and managers of the household. In many Middle Eastern and Islamic communities, the Kholah or Hajjat Al-Bayt (Lady of the house) is the matriarch of the family, responsible for maintaining a harmonious household, caring for her family's physical and emotional needs, and creating a warm and welcoming home environment. The title Kholah is a mark of respect and appreciation for a woman's role as the heart of the family.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kholah also holds spiritual significance as it represents the feminine aspect of Allah (SWT) in the Islamic tradition. In Islam, Allah is both a masculine and feminine deity, and the various names and titles given to Allah symbolize different aspects of His infinite attributes. The name Khala (feminine form of Kholah) is considered a title for the "Mother of all Believers," Maryam (mother of Prophet Isa/Jesus, as), and other revered women in Islamic history. Therefore, the name Kholah signifies the nurturing and compassionate aspects of Allah and the important role that women play in caring for and nourishing families both in this world and in the hereafter.
